topic: Neck and shoulder tension for new parents

slides.headline: New baby, neck up by your ears?
slides.sub: Why new parents carry so much tension, and small ways to ease it.

slides.title: Why it creeps up on you
slides.body: Feeding, rocking, settling and carrying a capsule all keep your head down and arms in front for hours. Add broken sleep and it's no surprise your neck and shoulders feel tight.

slides.title: Swap sides and positions
slides.body: Alternate the arm you carry on, the side you feed from if you can, and the chair you use. Small changes spread the load so one side isn't doing all the work.

slides.title: Bring baby up, not your head down
slides.body: Use pillows to raise baby during feeds so you can sit back with your shoulders relaxed. A footstool can help too. Look down with your eyes, not only your neck.

slides.title: What remedial massage can offer
slides.body: Massage can help tight muscles feel easier and give you an hour to yourself. It works well alongside gentle movement and strengthening, rather than replacing them.

slides.title: When to see someone else first
slides.body: Pain spreading down the arm, pins and needles, headaches that keep building or wrist pain that stops you lifting baby are worth a physio or GP assessment.

slides.headline: Carrying more than just the baby?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists work on neck and shoulder tension and share simple tips for your feeding and carrying routine.

caption:
New parent and your shoulders have moved up to your ears? You're in good company.

Feeding, rocking and carrying keep your head down and arms forward for hours, usually on very little sleep. A few small changes can help: swap the arm you carry on, raise baby on pillows during feeds so you can sit back, and look down with your eyes rather than your whole neck.

Remedial massage can help tight muscles feel easier, and it pairs well with gentle movement. Arm pins and needles or building headaches are worth a physio or GP check.
